title: What food safety training does ADAFSA require for food handlers in Abu Dhabi?
description: What Abu Dhabi's food safety authority (ADAFSA) requires for food handler training: Decree No. (6) of 2020, the mandatory EFST program, HACCP and records.
shortAnswer: In the Emirate of Abu Dhabi, the Abu Dhabi Agriculture and Food Safety Authority (ADAFSA) requires every food establishment official to ensure food handlers are trained in food safety and good hygiene practices and obtain the food safety training programs the Authority determines (Decree No. (6) of 2020, Article 3(c)). The baseline program is Essential Food Safety Training (EFST), which ADAFSA guidance describes as mandatory for all food handlers, managers and supervisors.
keyTakeaways: Decree No. (6) of 2020 issuing the food hygiene system during the food chain stages replaced Regulation No. (6) of 2010 and applies to all food establishments at every stage of the food chain.
Article 3(c) makes the food establishment official responsible for training food handlers and for ensuring they obtain the food safety training programs determined by ADAFSA.

ADAFSA Guideline No. (13) of 2022 describes EFST, launched in 2008, as a mandatory training requirement for everyone working in food handling in Abu Dhabi, including operators, managers and supervisors, ending in an ADAFSA approved exam.
Article 97 requires a food safety management system based on HACCP principles, and ADAFSA's design guideline expects food handlers to be trained in both EFST and HACCP principles.

Director General Decision No. (18) of 2020 phased the HACCP articles in: chains, caterers, hospital kitchens, labor camp kitchens and hypermarkets had up to one year, while listed small businesses use the Salamat Zadna manual.
jurisdiction: United Arab Emirates: Emirate of Abu Dhabi
regulator: Abu Dhabi Agriculture and Food Safety Authority (ADAFSA)
appliesTo: All food establishments in the Emirate of Abu Dhabi handling food at any stage, from primary production and manufacturing to storage, transport, display, sale and donation
Food establishment officials (food business operators), who carry the training duty
All food handlers, including managers and supervisors of food handling operations
Food service and retail businesses covered by ADAFSA guidelines and codes of practice

sections.heading: Which law sets food handler training duties in Abu Dhabi?

blocks.text: The core instrument is [Decree of the Chairman of the Board of Directors of ADAFSA No. (6) for the year 2020](https://www.adafsa.gov.ae/CMS/RegulationsAndDecrees/Decree%20No.%20(06)%20for%20the%20year%202020.pdf) issuing the food hygiene system during the food chain stages. It was issued on March 10, 2020, came into effect six months after publication in the Official Gazette (Article 107), and revoked Regulation No. (6) of 2010 on food hygiene (Article 106). It sits under Law No. (2) of 2008 regarding food in the Emirate of Abu Dhabi and Law No. (7) of 2019 establishing ADAFSA, both listed on ADAFSA's [legislation pages](https://www.adafsa.gov.ae/en/policies/Pages/regulations-and-decisions.aspx).

Article 2 sets a wide scope: the system applies to all food establishments that handle food at any stage, including primary production, manufacturing, preparation, packaging, transport, storage, display, sale and donation. That means farms supplying food, central kitchens, delivery operators and retailers are all inside the training duty, not only restaurants.

ADAFSA publishes an English translation of the Decree and notes on its cover that the translation is for non Arabic speakers and that the Arabic legislation is legally binding. Training materials should cite article numbers rather than paraphrased English wording where precision matters.

sections.heading: What exactly must the food establishment official do about training?

blocks.text: The food establishment official must make sure every food handler is trained and holds the training ADAFSA specifies. Article 3(c) of Decree No. (6) of 2020 obliges the official to "ensure that food handlers are trained in the necessary knowledge and skills in the field of food safety and good hygiene practices, as well as that they obtain food safety training programs determined by the authority".

The same article ties training to health and fitness duties that staff need to understand. Article 3(d) to (f) require the official to keep food handlers medically fit, maintain absence records, ensure they report symptoms promptly, and keep them out of food work until 48 hours after symptoms stop. These exclusion rules are a natural part of the induction content, because a food handler who does not know them cannot comply.

blocks.title: Who is the "food establishment official"?
blocks.text: The English translation uses "food establishment official" for the person legally responsible for the business, the role ADAFSA's earlier codes of practice called the food business operator. The training duty therefore sits with the license holder and management, not with the individual food handler.

sections.heading: What is Essential Food Safety Training (EFST), and who must complete it?

blocks.text: EFST is the baseline food safety qualification for anyone handling food in Abu Dhabi. Section 5.2 of [ADAFSA Guideline No. (13) of 2022 on food hygiene in the food service sector](https://www.adafsa.gov.ae/CMS/Guidelines/1072022.pdf) (published in Arabic) explains that ADAFSA launched the program in 2008 to give every food handler the opportunity to obtain a food safety qualification, and that it is a mandatory training requirement for everyone working in food handling in the emirate, including food establishment operators, managers and supervisors.

According to the same section, food handlers attend a course with accredited trainers, the course focuses on four core elements (cross contamination, cooking, chilling and cleaning), and after the training period the food handler must pass an exam approved by ADAFSA to receive the training certificate. The guideline reproduces a sample EFST certificate.

Retail is covered too. [Code of Practice No. (29) of 2019 on food hygiene for retail business](https://www.adafsa.gov.ae/CMS/Guidelines/292019.pdf), section 1.1.3, states that EFST "is a mandatory training requirement for all food handlers in Abu Dhabi Emirate" and that minimum training "may be followed by more specific training requirements, for those with greater responsibility in the business". That code was written under the revoked Regulation No. (6) of 2010 and describes EFST as run by the Abu Dhabi Quality and Conformity Council; the requirement itself is restated in the 2022 guideline, but operators should confirm the current delivery and certification route with ADAFSA.

sections.heading: Do Abu Dhabi food handlers also need HACCP training?

blocks.text: Yes, where the establishment must run a HACCP based system, staff need to understand it. Article 97 of Decree No. (6) of 2020 requires the food establishment official to develop and implement food safety management systems based on Hazard Analysis Critical Control Point (HACCP) principles, and Article 100 requires evidence of compliance proportionate to the nature and size of the business. [ADAFSA Guideline No. (6) of 2019 on food service design](https://www.adafsa.gov.ae/CMS/Guidelines/Guideline%20No%20(6)%20of%202019%20Food%20Service%20Design.pdf) asks, at question 5.10, whether food handlers have passed EFST and HACCP concept training, and answers that establishments "should have trained food handlers in Essential food safety training, and in HACCP principles".

The HACCP articles were phased in by business type. [Director General Decision No. (18) of 2020](https://www.adafsa.gov.ae/CMS/RegulationsAndDecrees/Decree%20No.%20(18)%20for%20the%20year%202020.pdf), issued April 5, 2020, set the following:

blocks.text: Those one year windows have long passed, so as at November 2026 these businesses should already be operating HACCP based systems with trained staff.

sections.heading: How should an Abu Dhabi food business evidence its training?

blocks.text: Inspectors will look for an EFST certificate for each food handler, HACCP training for staff operating critical controls, and records showing illness reporting is understood. blocks.text: Setting renewal dates is a local decision unless ADAFSA specifies one. [How to set mandatory training refresh cycles](/guides/how-to-set-mandatory-training-refresh-cycles) explains how to choose and justify an interval, and [how to build a training matrix for a food business](/guides/how-to-build-a-training-matrix-for-a-food-business) shows how to lay out roles against courses.

sections.heading: How does Abu Dhabi's approach differ from Dubai's?

blocks.text: Abu Dhabi builds its system around a universal food handler qualification (EFST) plus HACCP, while Dubai builds it around a certified Person in Charge on site and on shift. Both require training before or at the start of food handling, and both put the duty on the business rather than the employee. A group operating in both emirates will need two sets of certificates and should not assume one emirate's qualification is accepted in the other.

See [Dubai Municipality Person in Charge requirements](/regulations/dubai-municipality-person-in-charge-food-safety) for the Dubai model, and [food safety training requirements by country](/compare/food-safety-training-requirements-by-country) for a wider comparison. For workplace health and safety training in Abu Dhabi, which is a separate regime, see [Abu Dhabi OSHAD (ADOSH-SF) training](/regulations/oshad-abu-dhabi-ohs-training).

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry records each ADAFSA article and guideline section as an obligation linked to roles and assessment evidence, and flags where older codes of practice still cite the revoked 2010 regulation. That keeps EFST, HACCP and induction content traceable to the instrument currently in force.

faqs.q: Is EFST mandatory for every food handler in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.a: ADAFSA guidance says so. Guideline No. (13) of 2022 describes EFST as a mandatory training requirement for everyone working in food handling in the emirate, including operators, managers and supervisors, and Code of Practice No. (29) of 2019 says the same for retail. The legal hook is Article 3(c) of Decree No. (6) of 2020.

faqs.q: Is Regulation No. (6) of 2010 still in force?
faqs.a: No. Article 106 of Decree No. (6) of 2020 revokes Regulation No. (6) of 2010 regarding food hygiene during the food chain stages. Some ADAFSA codes of practice, such as Code of Practice No. (29) of 2019, still quote the 2010 regulation, so cross check article references against the 2020 Decree.

faqs.q: Does an EFST certificate need to be renewed?
faqs.a: The sources reviewed for this page do not set a renewal interval for EFST. Decree No. (6) of 2020 refers to programs determined by the Authority, so the renewal rule, if any, sits with ADAFSA. Confirm the current position with ADAFSA and record the answer in the training plan.

Guideline No. (13) of 2022 says the course focuses on four core elements: cross contamination, cooking, chilling and cleaning. Candidates attend training with accredited trainers and must pass an ADAFSA approved exam to receive the certificate.

faqs.q: Which businesses use the Salamat Zadna manual instead of a full HACCP plan?
faqs.a: Director General Decision No. (18) of 2020 lists individual establishments in hotels of three stars and below, establishments in educational institutions, tourist restaurants, popular kitchens and local restaurants. They apply the Manual of Safe Health Practices for Small Businesses (Salamat Zadna System).
